candidate_relations.reason: The clinical record confirms a retroperitoneal unilocular cyst on imaging and surgery, so C001 accurately captures the morphological finding. However, the reference diagnosis is filariasis — the parasitic etiology explaining the cyst (chylous/lymphatic cyst from filarial lymphatic obstruction), evidenced by the rural north India origin, spermatic cord thickening (filarial funiculitis), dilated lymphatics at the upper pole, and intermittent high-grade fever. C001 names only the anatomical descriptor without the etiological specificity required by the benchmark.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Describes the anatomical finding (retroperitoneal unilocular cyst) but omits the etiological diagnosis of filariasis, which is the requested final diagnostic object

case_quality_flags: Reference diagnosis 'filariasis' is an etiology; the full composite diagnosis would be 'filarial retroperitoneal lymphatic cyst' — the benchmark label is minimally specified but clinically grounded by spermatic cord thickening and dilated lymphatics in an endemic region
